practice_description.medium: Quantum computing, immersive video installation, VR, performance, generative imagery
practice_description.practice_summary: Libby Heaney is an artist and quantum physicist who uses quantum computing as a generative medium, exploiting quantum phenomena like superposition and entanglement to create artworks that exist in multiple states simultaneously -- challenging classical binary logic and offering new models for relational, non-hierarchical composition.
practice_description.methodology: Heaney holds a PhD in quantum information science from the University of Leeds and worked as a quantum physicist before transitioning to art. She writes custom quantum algorithms using IBM's Qiskit framework, running them on real quantum processors and simulators to generate visual and sonic outputs. The quantum processes introduce genuine indeterminacy -- outputs are not pseudo-random but reflect the fundamental probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics. Her work draws on art history (Hieronymus Bosch, Bruegel) and critical theory to frame quantum phenomena as metaphors and models for non-binary, entangled, relational ways of being. She has been artist-in-residence at the Goethe-Institut and has collaborated with quantum computing labs.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Heaney's use of quantum entanglement as a model for relational connections directly maps onto A(DAI)'s graph-based approach. Her work offers both a literal technology (quantum computing as generative medium) and a conceptual framework (entanglement as a model for non-hierarchical relations) relevant to graph-curated exhibition.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Yes -- quantum-generated imagery and processes could function as substrate layers in a generative composition. The outputs are inherently variable and indeterminate, making them ideal substrate material that resists fixity.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Strongly yes -- quantum entanglement is literally a relational phenomenon where particles are defined by their connections to other particles rather than by individual properties. Heaney's work treats entanglement as a model for how artworks, identities, and systems can be relationally determined.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Yes -- quantum processes are fundamentally indeterminate. Each measurement/observation of a quantum system produces a different outcome. The artworks evolve and recompose each time they are generated or observed, reflecting genuine quantum indeterminacy rather than programmed randomness.

works.title: Ent- (Venice Biennale)
works.description: Immersive multi-room installation at the 59th Venice Biennale featuring quantum-generated video projections, sound, and environments inspired by Hieronymus Bosch's 'Garden of Earthly Delights.' Visitors moved through three rooms representing different quantum states -- entanglement, superposition, and measurement/collapse. The imagery was generated using quantum computing algorithms that produced forms existing in multiple states simultaneously.
works.relevance: Landmark quantum art installation at the world's most prestigious art biennale. Demonstrates how quantum computing can drive immersive generative environments. The three-room structure models a progression through relational states relevant to A(DAI)'s Sense Room concept.

works.title: Elvis
works.description: Quantum computing artwork using qubits to generate glitching, morphing portraits that exist in superposition -- simultaneously multiple people, genders, and states. The work explores how quantum logic challenges binary categorization.
works.relevance: Demonstrates quantum indeterminacy as a creative medium for identity and representation that resists fixed categorization. The non-binary logic resonates with A(DAI)'s interest in knowledge systems that resist reductive classification.

works.title: Heart of the Entangled
works.description: VR experience where visitors enter a quantum-generated world and their actions affect the quantum state of the environment, creating genuine entanglement between visitor behavior and artwork evolution.
works.relevance: Interactive quantum art where visitor presence literally changes the work through quantum measurement. Models how observation/participation can be built into generative systems at a fundamental level. [uncertain]

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Heaney does not design governance protocols or institutional infrastructure as artwork, but she designs quantum algorithms -- computational protocols -- as creative medium. The quantum circuits she writes are protocols that generate art through fundamentally non-deterministic processes. This is protocol design at the level of physics rather than governance.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: Custom quantum algorithms and circuits written in Qiskit that serve as generative art protocols. These are computational systems that produce visual and sonic outputs through genuine quantum processes, not simulated randomness.

commons_orientation.licence_model: Unknown -- works are presented in institutional contexts (Venice Biennale, galleries); quantum code may be shared in research contexts but the artworks are not open source [uncertain]
commons_orientation.commons_summary: Heaney's practice engages with openness through the lens of quantum mechanics rather than legal/governance frameworks. Quantum superposition and entanglement model a kind of radical openness -- things existing in multiple states, defined by relations rather than fixed properties. However, the practice does not explicitly build commons infrastructure or use open licensing models.

governance_model.governance_detail: Heaney is the sole artist and decision-maker, designing quantum algorithms and directing the artistic output. She collaborates with quantum computing labs and institutions but retains artistic control. The quantum processes themselves introduce a form of 'non-human governance' -- the indeterminacy of quantum measurement means the final output is not fully controlled by anyone.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Not directly applicable -- the work does not use data from other people or communities. The quantum processes generate original imagery rather than transforming existing human data.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Hybrid human-machine co-authorship. Heaney designs the quantum algorithms, but the quantum computer's inherent indeterminacy means the machine contributes genuinely unpredictable elements. This is perhaps the most literal form of machine co-authorship in art -- quantum randomness is not pseudo-random but fundamentally indeterminate.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Each run of the quantum algorithm produces different outputs due to quantum indeterminacy. Installations can generate continuously varying imagery and sound. The VR works respond to visitor input. However, the underlying quantum algorithms are designed and fixed by the artist -- it is the quantum measurement that introduces variation.

data_materiality.data_sources: Quantum states generated by real quantum processors (IBM Quantum); art historical imagery (Bosch, Bruegel) as conceptual and visual reference; the quantum vacuum itself as a generative source.
data_materiality.data_provenance: Self-generated through quantum computation -- no scraped, borrowed, or ethically complex data sources. The quantum processes generate original outputs. Art historical references are used conceptually/visually rather than as training data.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Heaney's work operates in quantum state spaces rather than classical embedding/latent spaces, but there is a deep structural parallel: quantum state spaces are high-dimensional spaces where information is encoded in continuous superpositions, analogous to how neural network latent spaces encode information in continuous vectors. The key difference is that quantum superposition is physically real, not a mathematical abstraction over data.
embedding_space_relevance.multimodal: Yes -- works span visual (quantum-generated imagery, video), sonic (quantum-generated sound), spatial (immersive installation, VR), and interactive modalities. The quantum algorithms can drive multiple output modalities from the same quantum state.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Large-scale immersive installations with video projection, spatial sound, and sometimes VR. Ent- at Venice Biennale occupied multiple rooms that visitors moved through sequentially, each representing a different quantum state. Environments are dark, enveloping, and designed to create a sense of being inside a quantum system -- boundaries between self and environment dissolve.

interoperability.composability: Moderate -- the quantum algorithms could theoretically generate outputs for other systems, and quantum-generated imagery/sound could serve as inputs for other generative processes. However, the works are currently presented as self-contained installations rather than composable modules.
interoperability.technical_openness: Partially open -- Heaney uses IBM's open-source Qiskit framework and has shared aspects of her quantum art practice in academic/research contexts. The specific artworks are not open source, but the underlying tools (Qiskit) are. [uncertain]

technical_approach.stack: IBM Qiskit (quantum computing framework, open source); IBM Quantum processors and simulators; Python; custom quantum circuits and algorithms; video processing and projection; VR development (Unity or similar); spatial audio systems; image generation from quantum state measurements

network_position.scene_affiliation: Quantum computing research community; Venice Biennale / international art biennale circuit; UK digital art scene; science-art intersection; Goethe-Institut; institutional contemporary art (Schirn Kunsthalle, Light Art Space Berlin); quantum humanities/quantum aesthetics emerging discourse
network_position.connections: IBM Quantum (technology partner); Serpentine Arts Technologies (UK digital art ecosystem); broader quantum art emerging field; science-art institutions; Holly Herndon / Mat Dryhurst (shared interest in how technology structures creative practice, though different domains)

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Heaney offers A(DAI) a unique perspective: quantum entanglement as a literal and metaphorical model for relational composition. Her practice demonstrates how non-deterministic, relational processes can drive generative art at scale (Venice Biennale). She could contribute theoretical framing (entanglement as graph model), technical knowledge (quantum computing as generative medium), or artwork-in-graph (quantum-generated material as substrate in a generative composition).
